subject: Decision Making
subcategory: Famous Decisions That Changed the World
title: Rosa Parks Stays Seated
description: Learn Rosa Parks Stays Seated in one minute.

hook.text: On December 1, 1955, Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat to a white passenger. She was arrested.

buildup.text: Montgomery's buses enforced strict segregation. Black riders paid the same fare but had to sit in the back or stand.

discovery.text: Parks' arrest triggered a 381-day bus boycott. Black riders were 75 percent of bus revenue. The city's transit crumbled.

twist.text: Parks was not the first to refuse. Civil rights leaders chose her case because her reputation made her the ideal.

climax.text: Parks shows that a single act of refusal, at the right moment, with the right support, can break an entire system.

punchline.text: One seat, one refusal, one revolution. Timing and courage aligned.

quiz.question: Why was Rosa Parks specifically chosen as the face of the bus boycott?
options: She was the first to refuse
Her strong reputation made her the ideal plaintiff for the legal case
